findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the thing being tracked (for example, the request) and use it consistently, or add one sentence defining the stipend item as distinct from the request the first time it appears.
findings.violation: The section repeatedly uses the stipend item alongside the request and the stipend without ever stating whether the stipend item is the claim itself, the piece of equipment claimed, or another name for the request, so the reader cannot tell whether these are the same thing or three different artifacts moving through the same process.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence, 5 subordinate-clause markers: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 71 words with 5 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.

findings.evidence: The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter.
findings.fix: Name the actor as the subject: for example, the benefits team determines stipend eligibility before any payment goes out, and the benefits team escalates repeat requests automatically within the same quarter.
findings.violation: Both sentences in this section run their action through an abstraction (the determination, the escalation) instead of naming who determines eligibility or who escalates repeat requests, so the reader cannot tell which team or role is actually responsible for either action.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: Move subordinate clauses and modifiers after the main clause, not between its subject and verb.
findings.violation: At 71 words, with 0 comma-set-off clauses and 5 subordinate-clause markers, the sentence stacks interruptions between its subject and its main verb instead of holding the main clause together.

findings.evidence: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: End the sentence on the exception itself (that a role requiring fieldwork may claim a second device) and move the annual-amount tracking detail to its own sentence.
findings.violation: The sentence's newest, most important content, the exception letting fieldwork roles claim a second device, sits in the middle, and the sentence instead ends on a trailing detail about the second device being tracked against the same annual amount, so the reader's attention lands on the least important part of the exception rather than the exception itself.

findings.evidence: In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time.
findings.fix: Replace workspace stipend with the stipend or home-office equipment stipend throughout this paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph introduces the workspace stipend as a term for the benefit that every other section calls the home-office equipment stipend or the stipend, with no signal that the two names refer to the same benefit, forcing the reader to check whether a second, distinct stipend now exists.

findings.evidence: Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins.
findings.fix: Reformat the inline items as a numbered or bulleted list.
findings.violation: The sentence embeds three or more comma-separated parallel items inline rather than presenting them as a formatted list.

findings.evidence: Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date.
findings.violation: The sentence states a binding requirement using shall instead of must.

findings.evidence: The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount.
findings.fix: Restate the nominalized noun as the sentence's main verb: the finance office evaluates every submitted receipt.
findings.violation: The action is buried inside the noun evaluation, carried by the generic support verb conducts, instead of stated as the sentence's own main verb.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt.
findings.fix: Merge this section's content into How to Apply, or move it immediately after How to Apply.
findings.violation: This section restates the start of the application process that How to Apply already covers, but it is placed after Restrictions and Exceptions and Terminology Notes rather than beside How to Apply, so it tracks the order the document was assembled in rather than the sequence a reader applying for the stipend actually follows.
